title: One-step compatibility of the unused tape
statement: Let $M$ be a Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$ with zero work tapes, let $hk$ certify that its number of work tapes is zero, and let $x\in\Gamma^*$. For every configuration $c$ of $M$ on input $x$, taking one step of the machine with an added unused work tape from the configuration that preserves $c$'s state, input-head position, and output while adding a blank tape with its head at the origin gives the same result as first taking one step of $M$ from $c$ and then applying that configuration embedding.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$hk$ states that $M$ has zero work tapes
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a Turing machine over an alphabet $\Gamma$ with no work tapes, and let $M'$
be the machine obtained from $M$ by adding one unused work tape. For every configuration
$c$ of $M$ on an input $x$, one transition of $M'$ applied to the embedding of $c$ (same
state, input position, and output; blank added tape with head at the origin) equals the
embedding of the configuration obtained by one transition of $M$ from $c$; this also
holds when $c$ is halted.
